artifact.title: Airtel Plans $130 Million Investment in 40 MW of Data Centers Across Assam
artifact.content:
Bharti Airtel is expanding regional computing infrastructure in northeastern India through three planned data centers in Assam. The telecommunications company signed a memorandum of understanding with the state government on November 25, 2026, covering new developments in Jorhat and Silchar alongside an existing construction project in Guwahati. Reuters reported that Airtel's overall investment commitment is approximately ₹1,200 crore ($129.7 million), with 40 MW of combined planned capacity.

Three facilities, two investment figures

The largest commercial investment allocation is approximately ₹700 crore for the 15 MW Guwahati project, while Jorhat and Silchar share an estimated ₹500 crore, according to Business Standard. Assam's chief minister separately outlined a first-phase investment of ₹705 crore. The two figures describe different spending scopes and should not be added together.

The Guwahati facility is being constructed at Bongora's IT Park, with a March 2028 completion target. The other two projects are planned for four acres in Jorhat and five acres in Silchar, respectively. The government anticipates 164 direct jobs associated with the two newly agreed facilities. The company's broader completion expectation is 2028, rather than a guarantee of commercial service by a specific date.

Why regional data centers matter

Telecommunications operators can combine local computing with existing fiber networks to bring selected services closer to their users. Reducing the physical distance traversed by data can reduce propagation latency. Optical signals travel at roughly 200,000 kilometers per second through typical silica fiber, equivalent to about five microseconds per kilometer in one direction. Actual application response times also depend on routing, congestion, processing and the return path.

Multiple locations can also support replication and disaster recovery if engineers establish independent network routes, adequate backup power and suitable application architectures. Three buildings do not automatically provide three independent failure domains. Regional flooding, shared utility connections and common fiber corridors must be considered in the final design.

Power capacity and national expansion

The announced 40 MW is a capacity figure, not an operating measurement. If the three facilities collectively drew 40 MW continuously, their annual electricity consumption would be 350,400 MWh over a 365-day year. That calculation is illustrative only; the announcement does not establish whether capacity refers to gross facility input or usable IT load, nor does it disclose measured power usage effectiveness.

Airtel's March 2026 Nxtra announcement identifies a national expansion objective of 1 GW from approximately 300 MW, backed by a proposed $1 billion investment round. Assam's projects illustrate a regional approach alongside large campus developments such as South Korea's Ansan expansion.

Other infrastructure developments, including Bitdeer's Ohio proposal and Soluna's Texas development, demonstrate the importance of separating power commitments from operating capacity. Equipment selection, cooling reliability, network commissioning and customer service activation remain the practical milestones to watch in Assam.
